rigorous

RIG-er-us — contains 'rigor,' strict thoroughness; a rigorous test leaves nothing unchecked. · adjective

What It Means

Rigorous is extremely thorough, careful, and strict, allowing no shortcuts.

Only the most dedicated applicants survived the university's rigorous admissions process.

Example

Before a new medicine can be sold, it must pass years of rigorous testing: careful trials on cells, then animals, then thousands of human volunteers, with every single result checked and rechecked by multiple independent teams.

The process is thorough, careful, and demanding at every single step. Unlike 'quick,' which values speed, rigorous values thoroughness above all else, even if it takes far longer.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

thorough: Thorough means complete and careful in every detail — nothing on the list gets skipped. Rigorous adds strictness and demand on top of completeness: a rigorous process is not just full coverage; it holds every step to a hard standard and allows no shortcuts.

stringent: Stringent describes rules and standards that are strict and allow no exceptions — a stringent dress code, stringent safety limits. Rigorous more often describes the work itself: rigorous training or testing is thorough and demanding in how it is carried out, not just strictly worded.

exacting: An exacting task or teacher demands great care, effort, and attention — the demand is the point. Rigorous looks at the whole process: it is thorough, careful, and strict from start to finish, so an exacting standard is one ingredient of a rigorous program.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

lax: not strict or demanding enough

careless: not giving enough care or attention

Where it sits · how thorough the checking is — careful → rigorous → exhaustive

careful vs. rigorous: Careful is a milder word than rigorous — being careful just means paying attention, while rigorous implies an extremely strict and demanding level of thoroughness.

exhaustive vs. rigorous: Exhaustive can feel even more intense than rigorous: rigorous means strict and thorough, but exhaustive means leaving absolutely nothing at all unchecked or unexamined.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rig-

root — rig-: stiff (Latin)

suffix — -orous

suffix — -orous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin rigor ('stiffness, harshness') comes from rigere, 'to be stiff.' A rigorous process is, at its root, full of unbending strictness that allows no shortcuts.
